name: Standing Defense Strategy
description: Choose Alex Enriquez's takedown-defense material by distinguishing shots from space, established leg grips and standing ties.
summary: Alex Enriquez's Wrestling Takedown Defense For Grappling separates stance and sprawl study from specific leg attacks and tie-clearing problems.
overview: An opponent entering from space and an opponent already holding an elevated leg appear in different parts of this outline. Preserve that distinction when choosing a lesson; a general instruction to sprawl does not describe all the situations listed here.

products.title: Wrestling Takedown Defense For Grappling
products.blurb: The published outline separates initial leg attacks, established leg-control situations and clearing ties.
products.best_for: Grapplers choosing a wrestling-defense lesson that matches the stage of the standing exchange.
products.study_focus: Start with MAIN PRINCIPLE OF TAKEDOWN DEFENSE, then compare the from-space and elevated-leg entries in LEG ATTACK DEFENSE.

guide.display_title: Standing Defense: Alex Enriquez's Takedown Study Guide

fits: You need to distinguish defending the initial shot from dealing with a leg already controlled.
You want one reference covering wrestling stance, common leg attacks and clearing ties.
consider_alternative_if: The takedown has ended and your recurring problem is escaping a pin: the Danaher Pin Escape Fundamentals guide starts closer to that problem.

includes: Opening material covers stance, motion, sprawl and defensive principles, followed by stance and head-blocking drills.
The leg-attack section lists singles and doubles from space, elevated-leg situations, ankle picks, low singles, fireman's carry and dogfight cases.
The tie-clearing section covers head and hip position, the whizzer/overhook, front-headlock throws and single or double underhooks.
limits: The advertised curriculum concerns wrestling defense for grappling; it does not set out a gi grip-fighting or competition guard-pull decision curriculum.
The public list names drills without describing their execution or partner constraints.

start_here.title: Compare the entry with the established grip
start_here.task: In one recorded standing exchange, pause before contact with the legs and again after a leg is secured. Note which frame matches your actual difficulty. Compare Double Leg Defense From Space or Single Leg Defense From Space with the two elevated-leg entries in the outline; if the decisive control is an upper-body tie, locate that tie in Defending and Clearing Ties instead. Use the selected starting condition to choose what to watch, without inferring the defensive movement from its title.
start_here.section: LEG ATTACK DEFENSE: DOUBLE LEG DEFENSE FROM SPACE; SINGLE LEG DEFENSE FROM SPACE; SINGLE DEFENSE ON ELEVATED LEG: BETWEEN LEGS; SINGLE DEFENSE ON ELEVATED LEG: ANKLE TRAPPED IN ARMPIT
